children: Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, rise after stronger-than-expected retail sales data for August. Monthly retail sales rose 0.5%, after a 0.5% contraction in July, above the consensus forecast of a 0.1% contraction in a WSJ poll. "[U.K.] consumers continue to demonstrate a strong willingness to spend on the high street, despite high energy prices and the prospects of tighter monetary policy," Pantheon Macroeconomics' Rob Wood and Elliott Jordan-Doak say in a note. Ten-year gilt yields rise 2.1 basis points to last trade at 5.238%, Tradeweb data show. Gilt yields fell on Thursday after the Bank of England kept rates unchanged and said it would no longer sell very long-dated gilts under its quantitative tightening program. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
